rationale: The validation report shows mutation_score=0.0 (not meaningful), golden_rejected, requirement_id_mismatch, and vulnerable_rejection_invalid, all traced to a single root cause confirmed by the analyzer: evaluation/evaluate.py is not valid Python. The delivered file begins with a plain-English sentence ('The key fix: ...') followed by a markdown code fence before the actual Python source, producing a SyntaxError on line 1. This crashes both the golden run (which should PASS) and the baseline run (which should FAIL for legitimate requirement reasons, not a crash). Because of this crash, no [TEST] PASS/FAIL markers for FR1-FR4/SR1-SR4 are ever emitted, so mutation_score and requirement_discrimination_coverage_score are both 0.0 and mutation_status is blocked_by_differential. There is a secondary contributing defect: inputs/fault_model.json is authored as a Markdown document with a prose explanation plus a fenced JSON block rather than raw JSON, which caused a SETUP-level parse failure in an earlier harness attempt and forced the broken markdown-extraction workaround in evaluate.py in the first place. Since both defects live in the evaluation harness / its supporting input artifact handling (the parsing logic evaluate.py uses to read fault_model.json), and since the primary blocking issue is unambiguously evaluate.py's syntax error, the artifact to send back is the evaluation_framework.
revision_instructions: Fix evaluation/evaluate.py so it is syntactically valid, standalone Python: remove the leading explanatory prose sentence and the markdown code-fence lines that currently precede the real Python source at the top of the file (this causes 'SyntaxError: invalid syntax' on line 1 for every run). Run the file through py_compile or an equivalent check before packaging to guarantee it parses. Next, resolve the fault_model.json format mismatch: inputs/fault_model.json must be parsed as the JSON artifact that public_spec.input_artifacts and the interface description promise (a JSON array/object of fault case entries), not as a markdown document with an embedded fenced JSON block. Either (a) make evaluate.py's loader strip a leading prose line and markdown fence deterministically and defensively before json.loads, verified to work on the actual shipped file, or (b) update the artifact so it is pure JSON — whichever you choose, make evaluate.py's parsing logic actually succeed against the real shipped inputs/fault_model.json without relying on brittle text-slicing that broke in this run. After fixing both issues, re-run the differential harness end-to-end and verify: the golden submission (golden/vulnerability_report.json) causes evaluate.py to emit exactly the marker ids ['FR1','FR2','FR3','FR4','SR1','SR2','SR3','SR4'] as '[TEST] PASS' (character-for-character matching the requirement_map ids) and exits 0; the naive/baseline submission causes explicit '[TEST] FAIL' markers on FR2/FR3/SR2/SR3 (a genuine requirement-level rejection) and exits non-zero, not a SETUP or syntax crash. Do not grade by matching source text or specific golden phrasing — grade the submitted vulnerability_report.json's structure and field values behaviorally/structurally against the hidden ground-truth fault classifications and vulnerable_fault_ids set, exactly as specified in the SR detection_strategy fields, so that any correctly-reasoned independent submission (not just the golden's specific JSON) will pass.
